title: Frankie Dusen, Algiers violinists, Robichaux and Bocage
summary: Brownlee does not know Dusen, then recalls violinists Robichaux, Charlie Devergis, Al Minetta and Pete Bocage, and the Charlie Love records.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: What about, uh, Frankie Doosan, the colored trombone player from Al Jaze? Did you ever hear him? I just wondered.
It must be since my time, huh? Or how, how, is he an old timer?

I'm sure you heard him. Well, it might be just, I, I, no doubt I heard him, just like I was talking about Kid Thomas and I was talking about somebody else. Uh. Peter Volcage. Well, Peter Volcage, yeah, well, he was, he was all right. And then there used to be a violinist, too, that was quite a, one of them that lived in Al Jaze, he was similar to this left-hand violin player in the Lyric Theater and-
Robichaux. He played style like he did. He was very good.
Where did he live that they called the violin player, do you remember?
Well, he lived somewhere in Al Jaze, whether, whether, whether- Charlie DeVergis. DeVergis. Charlie DeVergis.
And Professor Minetta, who talked about him.
Well, yeah, Al Minetta, yeah. He played violin. He played violin, played well. And Bocas played violin, too. Yeah, I was going to say, I thought that Pete played violin as well. Still does. Uh-huh.

And do you know Charlie Love? He's a trumpet player from all that college, you know what, anyway? I don't remember. He and Bocas made some records where Bocas plays the violin and Love plays the trumpet. And they played some of the Red Book ragtime arrangements like Maple Leaf and-
